messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: elevated tail latency for generation API in prod-east. Signal: token-queue throttle + increasing request backlog. Automated severity: SEV3. Paging oncall.

miguel: got the page, I'm on it. starting quick triage — checking quota/token-bucket stats and recent deploys.

sara: I'm looking at runtime metrics now. token-bucket refill rates look normal, but per-tenant token spend has spiked on a small subset of customers (bursty batch jobs). backlog concentrated on edge-proxy group eu-west-2 -> prod-east routing path.

james: can we temporarily loosen per-tenant bursts? or move affected tenants to a soft-limit policy?

miguel: doing an emergency policy override to allow short-term bursts for 5m on affected tenants. applying: `rbac:update-tenant-burst --tenants X,Y,Z --burst 2x --ttl 300s`

eve: FYI there's a minor routing flake on the proxy that amplifies backlog under burst. I'm toggling proxy pool to add two warm nodes for prod-east.

ops-bot: Deploy note: `autoscaler` triggered +2 warm nodes in prod-east pool at 4861230120.

amy: heads-up for CS: some customers may see requests queueing or 10-20s slower responses. Draft customer note below, pls review: "We're investigating intermittent slow responses for text-generation in prod-east. We've applied temporary burst increases and added capacity; we'll update within 30 minutes."

kyle: good start, add CTA: customers can route to eu-central region as fallback temporarily, add link to status page.

sara: mitigation summary for status page: "Mitigation in progress: increased per-tenant burst allowance, provisioned warm nodes to proxy pool, rerouted low-priority jobs to batch queue. Observed initial improvements to queue depth but tail latency still off target."

miguel: current action items: 1) monitor queue depth and refill rates 2) validate proxy warm nodes healthy 3) patch a short-circuit to drop extremely large multi-prompt requests (opt-out) 4) prepare rollback for policy override. I'm assigning to self & sara.

james: adding runbook snippet for handoff/next steps: ```
- Check /metrics/token_queue_depth by tenant
- If depth > 500 for >5m: increase warm nodes, escalate to infra
- If refill rate < expected: check KMS latency and throttles
- If severe degradation persists >20m: open SEV2 and notify execs
```

eve: deployed quick filter to cap requests > 2k tokens to low-priority path (non-disruptive). logs show ~1% of requests were >2k and were causing disproportionate KV cache churn.

ops-bot: STATUS UPDATE posted to internal bridge at 4861230450.

amy: customer note v2 (short): "We've applied temporary capacity and policy changes to address intermittent slow responses in prod-east. If you experience degraded performance, please try our eu-central fallback or contact support@redwood.ai. We'll post another update in 30 minutes."

kyle: approve. Add link to status.redwood.ai/incidents/4861230000 when ready.

miguel: evidence so far: queue depth down ~40% in 10m, tail latency p99 improved from ~2.4s to ~1.1s but p999 still elevated. Keeping page open, ETA for stable recovery 30-45m assuming no new bursts.

sara: follow-up tasks for postmortem: trace top offending tenants, evaluate quota configuration, and add automated soft-fallback to route very large requests to dedicated batch tier.

james: handing off to night oncall @miguel -> @sara in 20m. miguel to update the incident postmortem template with timeline.

miguel: leaving notes for handoff: current mitigations active, monitor token_queue_depth, warm nodes healthy, policy override will auto-revert at 4861230300 (5m TTL) — I extended to 4861230600. contact page-owner `#infra-notify` if TTL expires and issues persist.

amy: sending customer-facing update now. copying status page link and short blurb to CS Ops channel.

ops-bot: CUSTOMER UPDATE posted to status page (public) at 4861230605. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4861230000.

miguel: closing notes: if we hit new burst patterns, we'll open SEV2. for now keep monitoring and collect logs for 24h retention for affected tenants.

sara: thanks all — I'll start the post-incident checklist and a draft internal comms template for execs highlighting impacted tenants, mitigations, and long-term fixes.

kyle: great job, quick and measured. :thumbsup:
